reason: E1 directly demonstrates the claimed dual-mode mechanism and ultralow wear in a Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 alloy, but it does not provide evidence that the same mechanism will operate in a CoCrFeNi matrix or that minor Ti/Nb additions will produce the required nanoprecipitate architecture in that system. E2 is unrelated to the hypothesis. Thus, the core mechanistic premises are supported only for a different alloy system, and the transferability and synthesis premises lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Nanohierarchical architecture with nanoprecipitates can yield ultralow wear rates from RT to 800 °C in a complex concentrated alloy
At low temperature, nanoprecipitates enable multiple deformation pathways that reduce friction and wear
At high temperature, nanoprecipitates promote a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer that minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear
Minor alloying additions (e.g., Ti, Nb) can form stable nanoprecipitates in a CoCrFeNi matrix
The dual-mode mechanism (stress partitioning + glaze formation) is transferable to a CoCrFeNi HEA matrix
